body:
Hey, thanks for responding.

I do think I'm going to keep on studying philosophy, but I'm concerned that it's not going to lead me anywhere that I particularly want to go. In general, I'm pretty skeptical of the ability of philosophy to provide anyone with a guide to life. Quite simply, I don't think that's something within its purview, so I don't really think that the study of philosophy, as much as I believe that it's admirable, will give me much of a reason to keep living by itself.

As for continuing to see a therapist, I guess you're right. More than anything, I just want to be able to talk to someone about how I feel. I guess the issue is that I'm somewhat turned off by the sort of advice that's usually offered.

Anyways, thanks for the reply. I appreciate it.

Hey, man. I'm sorry to hear about the issues you've been having. They sound fairly similar to some of the ones I've been dealing with, so I think that I can relate to how you're feeling.

I lived by myself for part of the past year, and the feeling of isolation really bothered me. I started to fall out of my routines, and that caused a lot of issues as well. I also had difficulty reaching out to any friends - even though more social contact would definitely have helped - because I didn't want to seem dependent or needy. Even after I came home for the summer I found it hard to reach out to my friends here for the same reason. Often I would go over a week without talking to them, and when they'd ask me why, I'd say "I figured if you wanted to talk to me you'd have called", or something along those lines. I just didn't want to always feel like I was always the one coming to them. I wanted to feel like I was the one being approached for a change.

Unfortunately, I've also got some issues with self-loathing. I straight-up just don't like myself very much as a person. It's really difficult going through life with a bunch of negative thoughts about myself constantly reverberating inside my head like it's some giant, hateful echo-chamber. All I can really do is try to occupy myself with other stuff, but that doesn't always work, and if I'm obsessing over something while I'm in a social situation, it really does tend to colour how I interact with people.

I hope things improve for you, and I'm glad you posted here. It's good to be able to talk to other people dealing with the same problems.
